rules: Never edit a migration file that has already been applied to production — create a new migration instead
Destructive change (rename column, drop column, change type) → requires a multi-step migration: add new → backfill → drop old. Never do it in one step on a live table
New NOT NULL column on an existing table requires either a DEFAULT value or a data backfill migration — test on a copy with production row counts before applying
Generated ORM client (Prisma, Drizzle) must be rebuilt after any schema change — type errors after a migration usually mean the client is stale, not that the code is wrong
Prisma migrations run via migrate deploy in CI/CD — never exec into the container to run them manually, or CI and production will diverge
_comment: Starter for any project with a managed database schema. Rules cover the universal failure modes: edited migrations, destructive changes, stale clients.
